newsitem.title: UK: Quieter Eurobonds see range of retail deals.
newsitem.headline: Quieter Eurobonds see range of retail deals.

text.p: Primary market activity slowed on Thursday, with issuance dwindling to a small trickle by the afternoon session.
Those deals that did surface, like a $200 million three-year bond for Bank Austria, were mainly aimed at retail investors.
"There is a bit of an overhang of supply, especially in short-dated dollars, so the market is taking a bit of a breather," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said.
"The short-dated dollar deals we are seeing are tapping into demand that will be generated by a large number of redemptions due on July 7," he said.
London emerging market specialists were preparing for a couple of significant roadshows -- Russia on Friday ahead of a jumbo dollar bond and China on Monday ahead of a mark deal.

Russia's $1.0 billion bond, due to be launched shortly after roadshows are completed on June 18, is expected to have a 10-year maturity after the good spread performance on recent Moscow and St Petersburg debut bonds.
Spread talk ranged between 350 to 375 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and 370 to 395 b.p. over, with traders expecting a yield of around 375 b.p. over Treasuries.
Russia's outstanding 2001 dollar bond was trading at 275 b.p. over on Thursday, compared with a 345 b.p. launch spread.
China is planning to launch a 500 million mark Eurobond via CSFB and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Elsewhere, the Philippine Central Bank said it could restructure the underwriting team for its forthcoming Yankee bond after banks gave conflicting advice on the timing and pricing of the long-delayed deal.
Salomon Brothers is lead manager, and co-lead managers are J.P. Morgan, Citicorp, Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley and ING Barings.
